title: Major depression: episode, severity and remission
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's depressive disorder.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for depression.

HPI
Pt is an 83 y.o. female presenting for f/u of major depressive disorder, single episode. Pt reports persistent low mood, profound fatigue, and difficulty with activities of daily living. Pt describes feeling "hopeless" and reports mood-congruent delusions regarding her health and mortality. Symptoms are persistent and have worsened over the last month. Pt denies any recent changes in medication adherence.

Medication List
Sertraline 50mg daily
Quetiapine 25mg qhs

Exam
General: Alert and oriented x3. Appears depressed and tearful.
Psych: Speech slow, coherent. Mood: Depressed. Affect: Constricted. Thought process: Linear. Content: Includes mood-congruent delusions. Insight: Poor. Judgment: Impaired.
Vitals: BP 132/80, HR 74, RR 16, Temp 98.6 F.

Assessment
1. Major depressive disorder, single episode, severe with psychotic features. Pt is currently experiencing a severe episode with psychotic features and requires continued close monitoring and pharmacological management.

Plan
1. Continue current medications. 
2. Increase Quetiapine to 50mg qhs to address psychotic features.
3. F/u in 2 weeks to monitor response to dosage adjustment.

Electronically signed,
P. O'Brien, PA-C
05/14/2026
explanations: Major depressive disorder, single episode, severe with psychotic features (HCC 152): F32.3.

distractors.why: Psychotic features are documented: they change the code and the HCC (152).
